```{r}

# Source figure options, packages, and main data prep.
source("./R/fig-opt-fun.R")
source("./R/packages.R")

```

To compare the multivariate Student's t models to the univariate counterpart (S13 vs. S18) we will use a more realistic simulation inducing correlations between variables and a larger data set (k = 12). Data are generated as having homoscedastic variance, including equal variance between groups (`sigma_ratio = 1` in `sim_wrap3`, see `R/sim-fun.R`), and added outlier noise. For comparisons, data included participant-level drop-out and values missing at random corresponding to about 10, 28 and 40% of the follow-up values with baseline values having about 8% missing values. Correlations were set to weak (independence between variables and time-points) and strong, about |r|=0.25 between measurement types and |r|=35 between time-points.  

As an example, the following synthetic data set was simulated using the simulation routine used in `R/model-comp3.R` (@fig-var-cor-synth). 

```{r}
#| label: sim-example

set.seed(2026)

k <- 12 # number of measurement types

# Grid cell from R/model-comp3.R: mid missingness (~28% of follow-up values,
# as in the trial data) and strong correlation.
ml <- list(dropout_int = -1.7, miss_prop_y = 0.05)
cl <- list(
  loadings_beta = matrix(c(2, 10, 1, 10, 1, 10), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE),
  c_corr = c(5, 10) # beta(5, 10) shape parameters, mean 0.33
)

d <- sim_wrap3(
  # Symmetric around 0 with a null spike so coverage is tested
  # for zero, negative, and positive effects.
  group1 = ifelse(runif(k) < 0.3, 0, runif(k, -0.4, 0.4)),
  group2 = ifelse(runif(k) < 0.3, 0, runif(k, -0.4, 0.4)),
  loadings_beta = cl$loadings_beta,
  c_corr = rbeta(k, cl$c_corr[1], cl$c_corr[2]),
  sigma_ratio = rep(1, k),
  N = 148,
  K = k,
  prop_noise = 0.025,
  sd_noise = 1.5,
  dropout_int = ml$dropout_int,
  miss_prop_y = ml$miss_prop_y,
  miss_prop_pre = 0.04
)

```

The missing data patterns from the medium sized missingness scenario corresponds approximately to the observed data (@fig-missing-synth, see also @sec-smodels-intro).

```{r}
#| label: fig-missing-synth
#| fig-cap: "Missing data patterns in the exemple simulated data set."
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| fig-width: 5.1
d$miss$raw_df |> 
    arrange(participant, time, type) |>
  mutate(miss = if_else(is.na(y), "miss", "obs"), 
         miss = factor(miss, levels = c("obs", "miss"), labels = c("Observed data", "Missing data"))) |> 
    mutate(.by = participant, 
         n_miss =  sum(is.na(y))) |> 
  # Reorder participants by missing values
  mutate(participant = fct_reorder(as.factor(participant), -n_miss)) |>
  mutate(.by = group, 
         participant_num = dense_rank(as.numeric(participant))) |> 


  # Per group
  ggplot(aes(type, participant_num, 
             color = miss, 
             fill = as.factor(type), 
             alpha = miss)) + 
  

  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2) +

  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(1, 0.6)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colscale) + 
  facet_nested( ~ group + time , scales = "free_y") +

  alpha_theme(yaxis = FALSE) +
  
  
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
        axis.ticks.y  = element_blank(), 
        axis.text.x = element_blank(), 
        axis.ticks.x  = element_blank(), 
        axis.line.x = element_blank(), 
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = c("gray90"))
        ) + 
  labs(x = "",
       y = "", 
       fill = "Measurement", 
       color = "", 
       alpha = "")
```

```{r}

# Some simulations have unsatisfactory chain convergence and ess statistics. 
# We will exclude these from comparisons and treat them as special cases
# where 500 + 750 iterations where not enough to capture the parameters.


# Extract hmc metrics to get a lsit of problematic data sets
files <- list.files("data-sim3/average_hmc_metrics")
ls <- list()
for(i in seq_along(files)) {
  ls[[i]] <- readRDS(paste0("data-sim3/average_hmc_metrics/", files[i])) |> 
    mutate(dataset = paste0("d", i))
}





p1 <- bind_rows(ls) |> 
  dplyr::select(name, m, model, variant, sim, miss, corr) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = m) |>
  mutate(flag = if_else(rhat > 1.1, as.character(sim), ""), 
         colflag = if_else(rhat > 1.1, "flag", ""), 
         corr = factor(corr, levels = c("weak", "strong")), 
         miss = factor(miss, levels = c("low", "mid", "high"))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(ess_bulk, rhat)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, 
             aes(color = colflag), 
             size = 3) + 
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = flag)) +
  alpha_theme() + 
  labs(x = "Bulk effective sample size (mean)", 
       y = "Rhat (mean)") +
  facet_grid(miss ~ corr, labeller = label_both) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("gray",colscale[2]))


# Excluded datasets (sim is unique over grid cells)
excl_datasets <- bind_rows(ls)  |>
  dplyr::select(name, m, model, miss, corr, sim) |>
  filter(name == "rhat" & m > 1.1) |>
  distinct(sim) |>
  pull(sim)

# Number of data sets
ndatasets <-  bind_rows(ls) |>
  distinct(sim) |>
  nrow()

n_excl_ds <- length(excl_datasets)


```


Using `r ndatasets` simulated data sets we are comparing models S13 to s18 for modelling performance using two scenarios of correlations (strong vs. weak) and three levels of missingness (low, mid, high). @fig-chain-diag shows chain diagnostics from the fits, no simulated data sets (n = `r n_excl_ds`) were excluded from comparisons due unsatisfactory chain convergence or effective sample sizes. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-chain-diag
#| fig-cap: "Chain dioagnostics under the full three by two simulated scenarios."
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 5.9

p1








```


For each estimate (treatment contrasts, 2 &times; 12 per data set), coverage of a 90% percentile interval was determined and averaged within each model, variant (full data and missing values) and simulation cell (missingness &times; correlation strength). With weak correlations, coverage of S13 was on avergae closer to the nominal level while S18 had slightly lower coverage. With strong correlations, both models had similar coverage, slightly below nominal at low missingness and close to nominal at mid and high missingness (@fig-sim-cred-int A). Credible intervals were wider in the missing data variant and widened with increasing proportions of missing values, while interval widths in the full data variant were similar across conditions (@fig-sim-cred-int B). With weak correlations, S13 had slightly wider intervals than S18 in both variants, consistent with its higher coverage. With strong correlations, interval widths were similar in the full data variant, but S13 tended to have narrower intervals than S18 in the missing data variant, a difference that increased with the proportion of missing values (@fig-sim-cred-int C).




```{r}
#| label: fig-sim-cred-int
#| fig-cap: "(A) Coverage of 90% credible intervals, (B) credible interval widths, and (C) differences in credible interval widths between models. "
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| fig-width: 5.9



# Extract coverage
files <- list.files("data-sim3/coverage")
ls <- list()
for(i in seq_along(files)) {
  ls[[i]] <- readRDS(paste0("data-sim3/coverage/", files[i])) |> 
    mutate(dataset = paste0("d", i))
}

# Combine coverage stats. Each sim is one data set (one grid cell), fit
# with s13 and s18 on the full and the missing variant.
ls <- bind_rows(ls) |>
  filter(!(sim %in% excl_datasets)) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("s13", "s18")),
         miss = factor(miss, levels = c("low", "mid", "high")),
         corr = factor(corr, levels = c("weak", "strong")),
         variant = factor(variant, levels = c("full", "miss")))


# Coverage per model, grid cell and variant
p1 <- ls |>
  summarise(.by = c(model, variant, miss, corr),
            coverage = mean(coverage)) |>

  ggplot(aes(miss, coverage, color = model, shape = variant)) +

  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
             size = 3) +

  alpha_theme() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.9, lty = 2,
             color = "gray") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(colscale[2], colscale[4])) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +

  labs(x = "Missing values",
       y = "Credible interval coverage",
       color = "Model",
       shape = "Variant") +
  facet_wrap(~ corr, labeller = label_both)


# CI width distribution per model, grid cell and variant
p2 <- ls |>
  summarise(.by = c(model, variant, miss, corr),
            m = median(ci_width),
            q5 = quantile(ci_width, 0.05),
            q25 = quantile(ci_width, 0.25),
            q75 = quantile(ci_width, 0.75),
            q95 = quantile(ci_width, 0.95)) |>
  mutate(grp = interaction(model, variant)) |>

  ggplot(aes(miss, m, group = grp)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95),
    width = 0,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +

  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
    width = 0,
    linewidth = 1.2,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +

  geom_point(
    aes(shape = variant, fill = model),
    size = 3,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +

  facet_wrap(~ corr, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 23)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(colscale[2], colscale[4])) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21))) +
  alpha_theme() +
  labs(x = "Missing values",
       y = "Contrast credible interval width<br>(Median 5-25-75-95% PI)",
       fill = "Model",
       shape = "Variant")


# Paired difference in CI width (s13 - s18) per estimate
p3 <- ls |>
  dplyr::select(time, type, sim, miss, corr, variant, model, ci_width) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model,
              values_from = ci_width) |>
  mutate(diff = s13 - s18) |>
  summarise(.by = c(variant, miss, corr),
            m = median(diff),
            q5 = quantile(diff, 0.05),
            q25 = quantile(diff, 0.25),
            q75 = quantile(diff, 0.75),
            q95 = quantile(diff, 0.95)) |>

  ggplot(aes(miss, m, group = variant)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
    width = 0) +

  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
    width = 0,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
    linewidth = 1.2) +

  geom_point(aes(shape = variant),
             size = 4,
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
             fill = colscale[3]) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0,
             lty = 2, color = "gray") +

  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22)) +
  labs(y = "Credible interval width difference<br>s13 - s18<br>(Median 5-25-75-95% PI)",
       x = "Missing values",
       shape = "Variant") +
  alpha_theme() +
  facet_wrap(~ corr, labeller = label_both)


p1 / p2 / p3 + plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A')
```



Accuracy was assessed as the error of the posterior mean of each treatment contrast (Estimate - Simulated). In the full data variant, the root mean squared error (RMSE) was practically identical between S13 and S18. Missing values increased the RMSE for both models, and the increase was smaller for S13 when correlations were strong (@fig-sim-error A). The paired differences in absolute error per estimate were centered close to zero in all comparisons and in both zero and non-zero effects, with wide distributions (@fig-sim-error B). S13 had the lower absolute error in a small majority of estimates in most comparisons (overall about 50-54%), with the largest proportions in the missing data variant with strong correlations (@fig-sim-error C).





```{r}
#| label: fig-sim-error
#| fig-cap: "(A) Root mean squared error (RMSE) of posterior mean treatment contrasts, (B) paired differences in absolute error between models (S13 - S18) in zero and non-zero effects, and (C) proportion of estimates where S13 had lower absolute error than S18."
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| fig-width: 5.9

# Extract error comparison (error of the posterior mean per estimate)
files <- list.files("data-sim3/error_comp")
ls <- list()
for(i in seq_along(files)) {
  ls[[i]] <- readRDS(paste0("data-sim3/error_comp/", files[i]))
}

# One row per estimate, model and variant
err <- bind_rows(ls) |>
  filter(!(sim %in% excl_datasets)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, type, model, sim, miss, corr, true, bias_full, bias_miss) |>
  pivot_longer(names_to = "variant",
               values_to = "error",
               cols = starts_with("bias_")) |>
  mutate(variant = factor(gsub("bias_", "", variant), levels = c("full", "miss")),
         model = factor(model, levels = c("s13", "s18")),
         miss = factor(miss, levels = c("low", "mid", "high")),
         corr = factor(corr, levels = c("weak", "strong")),
         effect = if_else(true == 0, "zero effect", "non-zero effect"))


# RMSE per model, grid cell and variant
p1 <- err |>
  summarise(.by = c(model, variant, miss, corr),
            rmse = sqrt(mean(error^2))) |>

  ggplot(aes(miss, rmse, color = model, shape = variant)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
             size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(colscale[2], colscale[4])) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
  labs(x = "Missing values",
       y = "RMSE",
       color = "Model",
       shape = "Variant") +
  alpha_theme() +
  facet_wrap(~ corr, labeller = label_both)


# Paired difference in absolute error (s13 - s18) per estimate
abs_diff <- err |>
  mutate(abs_dev = abs(error)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, type, sim, miss, corr, effect, variant, model, abs_dev) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model,
              values_from = abs_dev) |>
  mutate(diff = s13 - s18)

p2 <- abs_diff |>
  summarise(.by = c(variant, miss, corr, effect),
            m = median(diff),
            q5 = quantile(diff, 0.05),
            q25 = quantile(diff, 0.25),
            q75 = quantile(diff, 0.75),
            q95 = quantile(diff, 0.95)) |>

  ggplot(aes(miss, m, group = variant)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
    width = 0) +

  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
    width = 0,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
    linewidth = 1.2) +

  geom_point(aes(shape = variant),
             size = 4,
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
             fill = colscale[3]) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0,
             lty = 2, color = "gray") +

  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22)) +
  labs(y = "Absolute error difference, s13 - s18<br>(Median 5-25-75-95% PI)",
       x = "Missing values",
       shape = "Variant") +
  alpha_theme() +
  facet_grid(effect ~ corr, labeller = labeller(corr = label_both))


# Proportion of estimates where s13 is closer to the true value
p3 <- abs_diff |>
  summarise(.by = c(variant, miss, corr, effect),
            prop = mean(diff < 0)) |>

  ggplot(aes(miss, prop, shape = variant, color = effect)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
             size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, lty = 2, color = "gray") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(colscale[1], colscale[3])) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 15)) +
  labs(x = "Missing values",
       y = "Proportion of estimates with<br>lower absolute error in s13",
       color = "Effect",
       shape = "Variant") +
  alpha_theme() +
  facet_wrap(~ corr, labeller = label_both)


p1 / p2 / p3 + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.5, 1)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A')

```


Finally, we compared the error associated with data imputation. Overall, the RMSE was lower in s13 compared to s18 with larger benefit of s13 in imputation of pre-values and follow-up values under stronger correlations (@fig-sim-impute).

```{r}
#| label: fig-sim-impute
#| fig-cap: "(A) Root mean squared error (RMSE) of posterior mean imputed values, (B) paired differences in absolute imputation error between models (S13 - S18) for baseline (pre) and post-intervention (y) values, and (C) proportion of imputed values where S13 had lower absolute error than S18."
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| fig-width: 5.9

# Extract imputation error (error of the posterior mean per imputed value)
files <- list.files("data-sim3/impute_error")
ls <- list()
for(i in seq_along(files)) {
  ls[[i]] <- readRDS(paste0("data-sim3/impute_error/", files[i]))
}

# One row per imputed value and model
imp <- bind_rows(ls) |>
  filter(!(sim %in% excl_datasets)) |>
  dplyr::select(var, row, time, type, model, sim, miss, corr, error, coverage) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("s13", "s18")),
         var = factor(var, levels = c("pre", "y")),
         miss = factor(miss, levels = c("low", "mid", "high")),
         corr = factor(corr, levels = c("weak", "strong")))


# RMSE per model, grid cell and variable
p1 <- imp |>
  summarise(.by = c(model, var, miss, corr),
            rmse = sqrt(mean(error^2))) |>

  ggplot(aes(miss, rmse, color = model, shape = var)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
             size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(colscale[2], colscale[4])) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
  labs(x = "Missing values",
       y = "RMSE",
       color = "Model",
       shape = "Variable") +
  alpha_theme() +
  facet_wrap(~ corr, labeller = label_both)


# Paired difference in absolute error (s13 - s18) per imputed value
imp_diff <- imp |>
  mutate(abs_dev = abs(error)) |>
  dplyr::select(var, row, time, type, sim, miss, corr, model, abs_dev) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model,
              values_from = abs_dev) |>
  mutate(diff = s13 - s18)

p2 <- imp_diff |>
  summarise(.by = c(var, miss, corr),
            m = median(diff),
            q5 = quantile(diff, 0.05),
            q25 = quantile(diff, 0.25),
            q75 = quantile(diff, 0.75),
            q95 = quantile(diff, 0.95)) |>

  ggplot(aes(miss, m, group = var)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
    width = 0) +

  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
    width = 0,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
    linewidth = 1.2) +

  geom_point(aes(shape = var),
             size = 4,
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
             fill = colscale[3]) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0,
             lty = 2, color = "gray") +

  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22)) +
  labs(y = "Absolute imputation error difference<br>s13 - s18<br>(Median 5-25-75-95% PI)",
       x = "Missing values",
       shape = "Variable") +
  alpha_theme() +
  facet_wrap(~ corr, labeller = label_both)


# Proportion of imputed values where s13 is closer to the true value
p3 <- imp_diff |>
  summarise(.by = c(var, miss, corr),
            prop = mean(diff < 0)) |>

  ggplot(aes(miss, prop, shape = var)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
             size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, lty = 2, color = "gray") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 15)) +
  labs(x = "Missing values",
       y = "Proportion of imputed values with<br>lower absolute error in s13",
       shape = "Variable") +
  alpha_theme() +
  facet_wrap(~ corr, labeller = label_both)


p1 / p2 / p3 + plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A')

```


Together, although differences are small, these results indicate that S13 is at least as accurate as S18, with a modest gain in accuracy when correlations between variables and time-points are strong and data are missing.
